quests.instruction: Mat, sat and fat all end with -at. Which other word is in the -at family?
quests.hint: Look at the last two letters and say the ending sound of each word.
quests.explanation: “Rat” ends with the same -at as mat, sat and fat. Only the first sound is different in each word.
quests.funFact: Words in the same family rhyme because they share the same ending sounds.

quests.instruction: Change the first sound of “mat” to /s/. What new word do you make?
quests.hint: Keep the ending, and swap only the beginning.
quests.explanation: Swapping /m/ for /s/ turns “mat” into “sat”. The -at part stays the same.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT belong in the -at family?
quests.hint: Check how each word ends. Three of them finish the same way.
quests.explanation: “Vat” and “sat” end with -at. “Pad” ends with -ad, so it belongs to a different family.

quests.instruction: Add /r/ to the front of -an. What word do you make?
quests.hint: Put the new sound first, then slide it into the ending.
quests.explanation: /r/ + -an makes “ran”. “Rat” ends with -at and “run” ends with -un.

quests.instruction: Change “pan” to “pat”. Which sound changed?
quests.hint: Say both words and compare them from the start to the end.
quests.explanation: “Pan” and “pat” start with /p/ and have short a. Only the last sound changes, from /n/ to /t/.
quests.funFact: When only one sound changes, you get a new word. That is how word families grow.

quests.instruction: Which word belongs in the -an family?
quests.hint: Look at the last two letters of each word.
quests.explanation: “Tan” ends with -an. “Tin” ends with -in and “tap” ends with -ap.

quests.instruction: Which of these words would fit in a list with cap, map and tap?
quests.hint: Say the ending. Your lips close with a pop.
quests.explanation: “Gap” ends with -ap, like cap and map. “Gag” ends with -ag and “got” ends with -ot.

quests.instruction: Swap /j/ for /h/ in “jam”. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Keep the ending the same and change only the first sound.
quests.explanation: Changing the first sound turns “jam” into “ham”. The -am ending stays the same.
quests.funFact: Words in the -am family, like ham, jam and yam, all rhyme with each other.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT belong with ram, dam and yam?
quests.hint: Compare the endings. Which word’s last two letters are different from the rest?
quests.explanation: Ram, dam and yam end with -am, like “ham” and “jam”. “Ran” ends with -an.

quests.instruction: Add /w/ to the front of -et. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Round your lips first, then add the ending.
quests.explanation: /w/ + -et makes “wet”. “Web” ends with -eb and “wit” has short i.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the -en pattern?
quests.hint: Check the last two letters closely. Two of these words look alike.
quests.explanation: “Men” ends with -en. “Met” ends with -et and “mat” ends with -at.
quests.funFact: Word families like -et and -en help you read many new words quickly.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT rhyme with “get”?
quests.hint: Say the end of each word. Which one has a different vowel?
quests.explanation: “Pet” and “set” rhyme with “get”. “Got” has short o, so it does not.

quests.instruction: pin → pig → ___. Change the first sound of “pig” to /d/. What is the new word?
quests.hint: Keep -ig and change only the beginning.
quests.explanation: “Dig” keeps the -ig and starts with /d/. “Dog” changes the vowel and “din” changes the ending.
quests.funFact: The first sound of a syllable is called the onset, and the rest is the rime. In pig, p is the onset and -ig is the rime.

quests.instruction: Add /b/ to the front of -in. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Look at the vowel in the ending -in before you choose.
quests.explanation: /b/ + -in makes “bin”. “Bun” and “ban” have different vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word could join the list pig, dig and wig?
quests.hint: Drop the first sound of each word. Which one still sounds like pig?
quests.explanation: “Big” ends with -ig, like “dig” and “fig”. “Bag” ends with -ag and “bug” ends with -ug.

quests.instruction: Hop, top and mop all share the same ending. Which ending is it?
quests.hint: Say the three words and listen for the sounds that stay the same.
quests.explanation: Hop, top and mop all end with -op. Their first sounds are different.
quests.funFact: Pop, hop, top, mop, stop and shop all end in -op, and they all rhyme.

quests.instruction: Which word could join the list hot, dot and cot?
quests.hint: Say each ending slowly. Which one finishes with a tongue tap?
quests.explanation: “Pot” ends with -ot. “Pop” ends with -op and “pit” ends with -it.

quests.instruction: Swap /h/ for /l/ in “hot”. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: The ending stays the same. Only the beginning changes.
quests.explanation: “Lot” keeps -ot and has a new start. “Let” and “lit” have different vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word could join the list bug, rug and mug?
quests.hint: Cover the first letter of each word and compare what is left.
quests.explanation: “Tug” ends with -ug. “Tag” ends with -ag and “tub” ends with -ub.
quests.funFact: To tug means to pull something. A tugboat gets its name from the way it pulls bigger boats.

quests.instruction: Fun, sun and bun are all -un words. Which word with /r/ at the front joins them?
quests.hint: Put the new sound first and keep the ending the same.
quests.explanation: /r/ + -un makes “run”. “Rug” ends with -ug and “ran” ends with -an.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT belong with fun and sun?
quests.hint: Fun and sun share an ending. Which word does not match it?
quests.explanation: “Run” and “bun” end with -un, like fun and sun. “Bug” ends with -ug.

quests.instruction: cat → cap → cup. Now change the last sound in “cup” to /t/. What is the new word?
quests.hint: Think about which sound you are replacing. Only the ending changes.
quests.explanation: Replacing /p/ with /t/ in “cup” makes “cut”. “Cub” would change it to /b/.

quests.instruction: Change the vowel in “pot” to short i. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Keep the /p/ and the /t/. Swap the middle sound only.
quests.explanation: “Pit” has short i in the middle. “Pet” has short e, and “pig” changes the last sound as well as the vowel.
quests.funFact: A word chain changes one sound at a time: pot, pit, pat, pet.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words changes only the last sound?
quests.hint: Compare the first, middle and last sounds of each pair.
quests.explanation: “Pig” and “pit” share /p/ and short i. Only the final sound changes. “Pig” and “big” change the first sound.

quests.instruction: Which -am word names something you spread on toast?
quests.hint: Think of the food. Then check which choice ends with -am.
quests.explanation: “Jam” ends with -am. “Gum” ends with -um and “jug” ends with -ug.

quests.instruction: Which word is in the same family as “net” and “pet”?
quests.hint: Look at the last two letters and listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Jet” ends with -et like net and pet. “Jot” and “jut” have different vowels.
quests.funFact: Pet, net, jet, wet and vet all rhyme because they share the ending -et.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with -ap and begins with /n/?
quests.hint: You need both: the right beginning and the right ending.
quests.explanation: “Nap” starts with /n/ and ends with -ap. “Map” starts with /m/ and “nip” ends with -ip.

quests.instruction: Start with “mop”. Change /m/ to /h/, then change the last sound to /t/. What is your final word?
quests.hint: Make the first change, write the new word, then make the second change.
quests.explanation: mop → hop → hot. The first step gives “hop”, and the second step changes the ending to /t/.
quests.funFact: A word ladder changes one sound at a time. Mop, hop, hot is a tiny word ladder.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT belong with pen, hen and ten?
quests.hint: Look at the last two letters. Three words end the same way.
quests.explanation: Pen, hen, ten, den and men all end with -en. “Pet” ends with -et.

quests.instruction: Which group contains only -un words?
quests.hint: Check the ending of every word in the group, not just the first one.
quests.explanation: Bun, run and sun all end with -un. The other groups each have a word that ends with -ug.
